description: Implementation of Pilot Demonstration Models in order to introduce Piped Irrigation Modalities as a novel approach for Sri Lanka’s irrigation sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-11-10 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The persistent decline in crop yields due to prolonged droughts and the damages caused to the earthen canal systems as a result of increasing the intensity of rainfall have been identified as two major challenges faced by smallholder farmers in the dry zone of Sri Lanka. Therefore, it has been proposed to introduce piped irrigation water distribution systems instead of open type earthen canals which operate at low conveyance efficiency, as a solution to these challenges. Accordingly, a detailed technical study has been carried out to implement 04 pilot projects under 03 different piped irrigation modalities, covering an area of about 877 hectares, to demonstrate them as models. With the use of piped irrigation water distribution systems, it is expected to reduce the wastage of irrigation water from traditional open type canal irrigation systems, provide relief to farmers affected by water scarcity, direct smallholder farmers to high-value food crop cultivation, and increase women's participation in agriculture. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to implement 03 pilot demonstration models in the Northwestern Province and another pilot demonstration model in the Uva Province, using the funds provided by the Japan Foundation for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific (JFPR) for the benefit of the developing member countries of the Asian Development Bank and the funds amounting to USD 3.3 million provided  by the Asian Development Bank and another USD 1.68 million of the Government of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.
